name: Cosmic CRF Limited
sector: Cold-roll formed steel and railway/infrastructure components
summary: Real railway/engineering growth, but heavy reinvestment and a material prospective Amzen acquisition complicate owner economics. Parent revenue is scoreable; Supreme Court eligibility relief is recognized. Fully funded conditional models expose required finance and downside, while unresolved owner attribution and acquisition allocation keep final IAS NS.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Cosmic is a real but capital-intensive railway/engineering group, not a verified cash-return compounder. Parent revenue history supports a growth score, while acquisition-driven group growth requires separate treatment. The July Amzen LOI creates a far larger funding task than ordinary plant expansion. Supreme Court relief has restored eligibility; the remaining uncertainty is implementation, ownership and cash economics, not an unresolved adverse eligibility finding. Quality factors are scored selectively, but material owner-profit and acquisition-perimeter gaps prevent a final IAS.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: As of 20 October 2026. BSE SME 543928/COSMICCRF, ISIN INE0ORA01015, listed 30 June 2023. FY26 consolidated Ind AS with FY25 restated; parent history is explicitly separate. Amounts are ₹ crore unless stated. The secondary 19 October close of ₹1,088.90 is not live or an exchange-verified execution quote. Primary September capital is 9,502,643 shares, implying ₹1,034.74 crore equity value. The five-year investor horizon ends 19 October 2031, with FY27–31 plus a fiscal stub modeled from March balances and dated subsequent events. A 15% nominal equity hurdle and ₹5 lakh reference position are analytical conventions, not personal suitability advice. G2 holds final attractiveness; other gates remain Conditional.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: BQS 5.34; GQS and IAS NS. REV 8 uses constant-parent history; EARN and R remain NS for specific owner/perimeter gaps. D/P/L 2/3/8. Canonical weights, coverage and bounds are retained without reweighting missing factors. GOV 4, MOAT 6, REV 8, DUR 7, CAP 4, CASH 4, BAL 4 and EXEC 6 produce a fully supported BQS. The historical-revenue score is not erased merely by acquisitions. GQS retains its 85% scoreable weight and explicit missing-EARN bounds. R is not assigned from an existing-business counterfactual that omits the prospective acquisition perimeter. D and P incorporate the funded downside/valuation evidence; L is separately capacity-based. No small drafting discrepancy or legal allegation automatically causes a critical failure.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: The parent manufactures cold-rolled formed railway sections and fabricated products. NS Engineering, 74% owned at March, supplies sheet piles, poles and infrastructure products; Cosmic Springs, 91.70% owned, adds railway components and springs. FY26 parent sales of ₹333.8975 crore differ from group sales of ₹716.6003 crore. Subsidiary sales already consolidate in full, so buying the remaining NS shares cannot add revenue a second time. Commercial production began in February 2022 following a business transfer. Amzen is a separate prospective wagon-manufacturing acquisition, currently reported nonoperating in the July LOI, not an existing revenue source.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Customer qualification, consistent engineering tolerances and installed assets support a moderate moat. Steel processing remains competitive, and raw-material pass-through has a timing lag; regional/customer concentration limits pricing independence. Pennar FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹3,620.09 crore, owner PAT ₹138.81 crore and CFO ₹202.12 crore provide a larger engineering comparison, though ₹328.27 crore PPE cash purchases still exceeded CFO. Salasar revenue of ₹1,502.77 crore and CFO ₹72.63 crore show a different fabrication/EPC cash profile. Product mix, acquisition perimeter and lease accounting differ, so these are operating comparisons, not a mechanically averaged valuation multiple.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Constant-parent revenue for FY23/FY24/FY25/FY26 is ₹121.489/₹253.4769/₹301.637/₹333.8975 crore. Three-year CAGR is 40.07%; the latest two annual growth rates slow to 19.00% and 10.70%. The preferred available three-year history starts REV at 9, reduced to 8 for deceleration and consistent with the short-history/medium-confidence ceiling. The latest two-year CAGR is only 14.77%, an important contrary diagnostic, not a replacement selected for convenience. Group sales rose from ₹401.6323 crore to ₹716.6003 crore with acquired subsidiaries; this is not purely organic. Four September order disclosures total ₹35.3022 crore including GST, not recognized net sales or an additive verified current backlog.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: Disclosed current capacity is 133,600 MT and production 106,370 MT; the FY28 target of 174,600 MT is a plan, not current output. Existing-business scenarios cap demand by assumed utilization and realization, with ₹50 crore reference project spend plus maintenance. This expressly excludes Amzen. Its July LOI specifies ₹284 crore resolution consideration over 12 months, or ₹266.5703 crore within 90 days, following NCLT approval. May management commentary indicates roughly ₹400 crore total Amzen project spending including expansion. Separate linked branches finance acquisition, revival, incremental WC and interest. The target had nil FY25/FY26 turnover, so future production is assumed, not extrapolated reported earnings. Strategic deposits and related-unit advances are already paid and not added again as new cash uses.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: Promoter Aditya Vikram Birla and related entities control the group. Reported March promoter holding was 55.09%; MD and whole-time director remuneration rose to ₹1.38/₹0.45 crore from ₹0.87/₹0.30 crore. The auditor highlights material related procurement and capital advances as a key audit matter. Prilika-related rent, job work and purchases, plus a ₹9.75 crore unit advance, require commercial scrutiny without implying diversion. The proposed ₹96.430453 crore minority buyout includes related/other sellers and a valuation report; disclosure is not proof of an attractive price. August/September warrant conversions added 296,400 shares and ₹35.87922 crore remaining cash, and September shareholding confirms 9,502,643 shares with no outstanding warrants. The proposed further 725,041 swap shares were not in that pattern; later completion is unverified. Amzen’s LOI describes collective company/group/promoter ownership without allocating the listed company’s economic share. The 3 August filing reports a ₹5,900 paid BSE fine for a one-day related-party disclosure delay, attributed by the company to a portal glitch. This small paid procedural matter is not treated as misconduct or a separate gate failure.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
Reported FY26 CFO of ₹23.7598 crore follows restated negative ₹37.9710 crore. Receivables and inventory absorbed ₹91.3728/₹31.8722 crore, partly funded by ₹97.4218 crore payables. CFO less reported ₹132.9966 crore fixed-asset purchases is negative ₹109.2368 crore, only a proxy because leases, acquisitions and noncash capital movements require a bridge. FY25 original CFO/CFI/CFF of −₹72.5993/−₹65.1507/₹247.9550 crore restate to −₹37.9710/−₹145.9156/₹193.8516 crore. The aggregate ₹100.24 crore difference is the deposit-definition change, not a newly discovered loss. Original-layout equity/EPS review confirms that group PAT ₹50.5632 crore, retained-profit movement ₹38.3689 crore and minority movements do not alone reconcile owner PAT. No fraud conclusion is inferred.

Opening claims are mapped once. ₹119.5092 crore borrowings include ₹3.4924 crore preference carrying value; bank/other loan debt is therefore ₹116.0168 crore, with ₹4.9 crore preference face retained separately. Lease face ₹13.6062 crore differs from note total ₹14.5066 crore and maturity sum ₹14.5336 crore; the higher maturity sum is used with a face-value sensitivity. Only ₹8.2572 crore is free cash. ₹102.3907 crore deposits are separately released by assumption, and ₹0.0536 crore pledged deposit is not netted. ₹30.848 crore advances recoverable in cash/kind are neither free cash nor automatically recovered. Actual operating WC is ₹158.7578 crore. Net current tax ₹4.3608 crore, current employee amounts ₹0.0849 crore and accrued borrowing interest ₹0.1305 crore settle once. Ordinary statutory/employee/expense/customer dues remain within WC. Noncurrent employee ₹0.0804 crore and deferred tax ₹4.905 crore remain terminal claims. No noncash lease creation is treated as financing cash.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
The dated equity value is ₹1,034.74 crore; no precise owner P/E is asserted. The existing-business counterfactual uses growth 4%/14%/23%, margins 9%/11.5%/14%, WC 36%/28%/24%, and exit 6×/9×/12×. It deducts the subsequently reported ₹31.60 crore cash deposit once, assumes no recovery or target value, and does not treat the ₹28.40 crore BG as cash spent. Bear/base/bull prices are ₹174.37/₹1,179.04/₹2,520.33 with annualized returns −30.67%/1.60%/18.28%; peak bank debt is ₹248.82/₹116.02/₹116.02 crore. Base 12%/15%/18% hurdle entries are ₹669.02/₹586.19/₹515.37, mathematical outputs rather than executable limits.

Separate Amzen branches fund ₹284 crore acquisition less an assumed ₹1.75 crore already-paid EMD offset, plus ₹116 crore revival/build cash. The August ₹31.60 crore is within, not additional to, acquisition cash. An explicit no-offset alternative prevents assuming a documented credit. The illustrative target sales ramp is ₹0/100/350/600/800 crore through FY27–31, 10% margin and 30% WC, all analyst assumptions; ₹800 crore corresponds to 2,000 wagons at an assumed ₹0.4 crore realization, not an order-backed forecast. This fully funded branch yields ₹1277.06 per share and 3.24% return but requires ₹605.82 crore peak bank debt. Slow/strong branches yield ₹782.65/₹2514.40; differing ownership, the NPV option, BG call and 20% dilution are separately modeled. At 50% target economics with all cash costs assigned to the group, return is −3.78%; this is a conservative allocation stress, not a claim about final ownership.

Annual models link revenue, WC, capex, depreciation, 26% positive-profit tax, old claims, bank and lease financing, preference dividends, cash floor and terminal equity. New draws incur half-year interest; repayments occur at year-end. No unspent FD, old advance or acquisition book asset is also added to enterprise value. Minority claims and proposed swap shares are explicit. Required draws are not committed capacity; actual October cash and target financing remain unknown.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
Permanent loss can arise from delayed collections, steel-price timing, underutilized plants and debt-funded revival, not just an earnings miss. The existing-business bear ends near ₹174.37 per share, approximately 84% below entry, with ₹248.82 crore peak bank debt; severe common equity is zero and peak bank debt is ₹358.24 crore. The separately funded stalled-Amzen case reaches ₹500.62 crore bank debt with no target sales. Deposits, working plants and verified equity receipts are counterevidence to immediate failure, but not committed expansion liquidity.

The disclosed ₹10.3334 crore Cosmic Ferro Alloys business-transfer claim remains an arbitration exposure at the annual-report date, not an established payable. The Supreme Court’s 14 May 2026 judgment set aside the challenged NCLAT orders and consequential actions and declared Cosmic eligible to participate in the Amzen CIRP; the resolution proceedings were to continue according to law. The July LOI then records CoC approval subject to NCLT approval. Eligibility relief does not itself prove acquisition completion, project success or a specified listed-company ownership percentage. The ₹49 crore NS corporate guarantee is not added again to already consolidated debt without a separate incremental-call assumption.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: At current issued shares, 5×/10× require terminal common equity of roughly ₹5,174/₹10,347 crore. At 20× owner earnings, this implies profit around ₹259/₹517 crore; at an assumed 8% owner margin, sales around ₹3,234/₹6,467 crore. The planned legacy capacity increase alone does not establish those outcomes. Separate acquisition capacity can expand the opportunity, but requires purchase consideration, revival, WC, finance and an economic ownership allocation. Even the strong funded Amzen illustration produces only about 2.31× the dated entry price. Five-year 5×/10× remains speculative, not a base expectation or assigned probability.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Require an issuer reconciliation of owner PAT, NCI, acquisition eliminations and noncash cash-flow movements. Track collection of ₹205.29 crore receivables, ₹107.86 crore inventory and supplier financing rather than celebrating reported growth alone. Verify usable deposits, bank/guarantee sublimits and actual interim debt. For Amzen, obtain the NCLT implementation order, chosen consideration option, deposit offset, BG collateral/call conditions, revival budget, commissioning and orders, and the listed company’s ownership/funding share. Confirm NS swap allotment and do not add subsidiary revenue again. Monitor strategic/Prilika advance recovery, arbitration developments, preference terms and lease reconciliation. Refresh actual-position BSE trading conditions before an execution decision.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Watchlist with a targeted evidence and investment-attractiveness hold, not a buy allocation. Cosmic has moderate industrial barriers and real production, but its capital allocation and funding perimeter are changing materially. A completed applicable review can retain NS where evidence genuinely fails to establish a single owner-economics baseline. The funded cases show consequences and required finance; they are not lender commitments or a disguised price target. No established misconduct, current default or trading prohibition is inferred.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Annual reports, primary results, credit rationale, capital/allotment filings, the Supreme Court judgment and Amzen LOI were read. Original equity, EPS, lease and claim layouts were checked before assigning a material reconciliation concern. September purchase-order originals update activity without converting gross orders into revenue. The August cash/BG payment is independently reproduced by public exchange-announcement indexes, but the BSE PDF retrieval failed; this source limitation is retained. Public issuer media and current index searches did not establish later acquisition/swap completion, which is not proof of noncompletion. Market history is secondary, dated and bounded. Remaining facts affect specific owner/funding estimates, not all established business-quality evidence.

conventions: Current audited face balances are the starting point; later ₹35.87922 crore warrant-conversion cash is added once in FY27. Initial warrant deposits already in March funds are not added again. No fabricated actual October cash/debt measurement.

New bank borrowing has half-year interest; ordinary repayment occurs at year-end. Cash tax and borrowing are solved jointly. Lease interest and principal are separate; no noncash new lease creation is treated as financing cash. Forecast replacement/new space is financed through cash capex.

Higher ₹14.5336 crore lease maturity sum is used conservatively against face ₹13.6062 crore and note total ₹14.5066 crore; the face-value sensitivity is explicit. These original-layout differences remain unresolved, not extraction errors.

Borrowings include ₹3.4924 crore preference carrying value, removed from bank debt and replaced by ₹4.9 crore face claim at terminal, plus 1% annual face dividend. These noncumulative redeemable shares are not treated as ordinary debt that excess cash automatically repays.

Current net income tax ₹4.3608 crore, accrued bank interest ₹0.1305 crore and higher face current employee amounts ₹0.0849 crore are settled once. Normal statutory/expense/customer dues remain in WC. Retain ₹0.0804 crore noncurrent employee claim and ₹4.905 crore deferred tax at terminal; no gross plan-asset double charge.

₹30.848 crore advances recoverable in cash/kind are excluded from operating WC pending nature/recovery reconciliation and are not assumed free cash. Their 0/50/100% recovery is separately modeled. CIRP and unit/capital advances are already paid and neither recharged nor automatically credited as cash or terminal value.

The ₹100 crore preference-issue FD is described as free in the December 2025 rating at March 2025, but later deployment/earmarking is unverified. Reference releases half of ₹102.3907 crore during FY27, with zero/full-release cases. No residual FD or pledged deposit is credited again at terminal. This is an assumption, not a verified restriction or loss.

Existing-business project cash capex of ₹50 crore reference/₹70 crore bull plus 2% maintenance excludes the prospective Amzen acquisition and revival. These counterfactual cases deduct the August ₹31.60 crore cash deposit once and assign it no recovery/terminal value; the ₹28.40 crore BG is not cash spent. Capacity ramps 154,600 MT in FY27 to 174,600 MT in FY28, with scenario utilization/mix limits.

Separate Amzen branches fund ₹284 crore acquisition less an assumed ₹1.75 crore opening EMD offset, plus ₹116 crore revival/build cash, approximately the management ₹400 crore total project indication. The ₹31.60 crore August payment is included within acquisition cash, never added again. No-offset and NPV-price alternatives are explicit. Payment timing is assumed FY27, not verified completion. Existing-business ₹50 crore project spending is additional. All required borrowing is mechanically solved, not committed. Target depreciation is assumed 5% on acquisition/build cost, not an audited purchase-price allocation. Target operating revenue/margin/WC ramps are analytical assumptions, with nil-sales stalled case. All cash cost is assigned to the listed group; 50/74/100% economic ownership scenarios expose unallocated promoter participation without inventing contributions. BG call sensitivity is a separate incremental-loss stress, not ordinary acquisition consideration.

Minority enterprise claims use disclosed subsidiary revenues and ownership under common modeled economics. They are not an exact owner-profit or subsidiary debt allocation. Separate 8/12/20% minority bounds retain this limitation.
The proposed swap removes only NS Engineering minority and adds 725,041 shares; no revenue or cash is created. Completion after September remains unverified, so main cases exclude it.

Additional arbitration/strategic/interest cash stresses are conditional loss/funding tests, not asserted adverse court outcomes or booked obligations. Main cases assume no fresh equity; the 20% equity sensitivity links proceeds and shares.
